To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of landmarks and contracts can improve the design and implementation of agent interaction in organizations.

1) landmarks are a useful concept to model and reason about the structure of organizations; and 2) contracts are a useful concept for modeling and reasoning about the goals and the behavior of agents in an organization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of multi-agent systems for organizations.
the design and implementation of agent-based systems that can be used in organizations.

the development of agent societies in which agents can collaborate in an autonomous way, i.e., agents are able to decide among each other on how they collaborate, but also on the basis of which goals and structure they collaborate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
landmarks and contracts are useful techniques to design agent societies.
the combination of landmarks and contracts is a promising approach to model and design agent societies, and to support the design process.
the presented techniques can be used to support agent autonomy in different agent society types, and thus are suitable for modeling and realizing organizations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of landmarks and contracts allows the design of agent societies with high collaboration autonomy and low organizational complexity.
we have developed a framework that supports the design of agent interaction by means of landmarks and contracts and that allows for the specification of agent societies and their interaction.
landmarks and contracts can be used to design agent interaction, but that they are not sufficient to model and support the whole organization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
landmarks and contracts can be used to support agent autonomy and to design agent interaction.
landmarks and contracts can be used to design agent societies that are flexible and autonomous.
the use of landmarks and contracts allows us to design multi-agent systems in which agents can be designed to be both organizationally compliant and autonomous.
